No, cold knife conization and LEEP (Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure) are not the same procedure, although both are used to diagnose and treat cervical lesions. 

Cold knife conization is a surgical procedure where a cone-shaped sample of tissue is removed from the cervix using a scalpel. It is typically performed in a hospital setting under general anesthesia.

LEEP, on the other hand, is an outpatient procedure where a thin wire loop is used to remove abnormal tissue from the cervix. It is usually performed in a doctor's office under local anesthesia.

While both procedures aim to remove abnormal cervical tissue for diagnosis and treatment, they differ in their approach, setting, and level of anesthesia required.
